title: Substitute hours-long retention bakes with infrared photo-stimulated screening
idea: Substitute multi-hour hot-bake retention tests with sub-bandgap (~1.3-1.6 um) LED illumination at wafer sort. The light photo-ionizes the deep traps behind tail cells and speeds up only defect-assisted leakage, so a scan of a few seconds yields retention maps per row and per mat.
why: A cheap, gas-free test step that makes retention-aware refresh and binning practical at volume: more usable supply and 4-8x refresh cuts.

title: Swap thermionic switching for heterojunction tunnel-FET access device
idea: Substitute the MOSFET's thermionic barrier with band-to-band tunneling: a p+ SiGe source on the bitline side, an intrinsic Si channel and a lightly doped n storage side. The device is asymmetric (it tunnels only when the wordline is high) and sub-60 mV/dec, and the lightly doped storage side suppresses ambipolar leakage.
why: Voltage floor + leakage: the steep slope lets VPP drop from ~3 V to ~1.5 V (~4x lower wordline CV^2 energy) while keeping fA-class off-current, so refresh activation energy falls too.

title: Weak-row CAM companion die on the DIMM buffer
idea: A 180 nm CAM-plus-timer die, or a block in the RCD buffer, holds the addresses of the ~0.1% weak rows found at test. It issues targeted extra refreshes for them while the DRAM runs at a 4-8x lower base refresh rate.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth fall 75-85%, and a legacy node is enough for a ~10k-entry CAM.

title: Ten people, one kernel module: retire weak pages, run 4x tREFI
idea: 10-person constraint: ship software plus a BIOS setting. A kernel module runs a retention test at 4x the refresh interval and retires the ~0.01-0.1% of 4 KB pages that fail (BadRAM-style memmap exclusion). It stores the compressed failing-page list in the DIMM's user-writable SPD bytes so the list travels with the module, then sets tREFI 4x longer.
why: Fact 3: cuts refresh energy ~75% and recovers ~8-15% of bandwidth for under 0.1% of capacity, on any server, with no new hardware.

title: Unified charge-debt counter for retention and row hammer
idea: Each row carries one counter that accumulates time weighted by temperature plus neighbor activations weighted by coupling. A row is refreshed when its debt crosses a threshold, so one mechanism handles both retention and hammer.
why: Replaces the fixed 64 ms sweep plus separate TRR. Quiet rows refresh 4-8x less often, and hammer victims (fact 9, ~1k ACTs) are restored exactly in time.

title: Selectron flood-holding: global photocurrent keeps nodes bistable, no refresh
idea: Revive RCA's 1948 Selectron and the Tektronix bistable storage tube, in which a continuous electron flood held each element at one of two stable potentials: a weak backside IR flood lets each storage node's photodiode supply a tiny current that balances leakage. A per-node negative-differential-resistance element gives the node two stable points (0 and VDD), so cells self-latch at picowatt levels instead of decaying.
why: Removes refresh as an operation (fact 3); standby power becomes flood power, targeted at under 1/10 of refresh power for 32-64 Gb dies.

title: Idle bitlines parked at the subarray's majority stored level
idea: Write logic keeps a per-row inversion flag so most cells in a subarray hold the same level. In idle, bitlines park at that rail instead of VDD/2, so majority cells see Vds~0 and subthreshold current, proportional to 1-exp(-Vds/kT), collapses.
why: More than 80% of cells see near-zero leakage drive, extending retention 3-5x and cutting self-refresh energy proportionally.

title: Laser-regrown epitaxial storage contact removes implant-damage leakage
idea: Worse: implant the storage-node junction and leave damage clusters that drive trap-assisted leakage. Flip: form the junction by in-situ-doped selective epitaxy followed by nanosecond laser melt-regrowth, giving a defect-free graded junction with no implant cascades.
why: Junction leakage tail (fact 3) about 10x tighter; longer refresh interval.

title: Wide-gap oxide drain pocket on a silicon access transistor
idea: The storage-node contact is an IGZO or Ga2O3 landing pad that forms the drain extension, so the high-field drain edge where GIDL is generated lies in >3 eV-gap material while the channel stays silicon for mobility.
why: Band-to-band GIDL dominates the leakage tail under negative-wordline bias, and a wide gap suppresses it exponentially. That could push the 13 fA tail below 0.1 fA, about 10x longer retention.

title: Deliberately weakened canary cells let dies refresh at true retention
idea: Box: standard cell x canary cells with a leakier access transistor made by one extra Vt-lowering implant mask x on-die canary sensing x per bank x Si x one mask. Canaries fail at ~1/4 of the weakest real cell's retention, so the die stretches its interval until canaries start failing, tracking temperature, voltage and aging live.
why: Replacing worst-case spec with live tracking typically allows 2-4x longer intervals, cutting refresh energy and bandwidth loss (fact 3) 50-75%.

title: Back gate merged as a second, slow wordline
idea: Build the array on UTBB FD-SOI with a ground plane per row group. Hold the plane strongly negative while the group is retaining (Vt +0.3-0.5 V) and swing it toward neutral only for the group being activated.
why: Decoupling on-current from off-leakage gives ~100x less subthreshold leakage. It also lets the wordline boost fall from 3 V toward 2 V, about 55% less CV^2 (fact 10).

title: Back-to-back refresh rows hand their wordline charge to each other
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging (in time): refresh is the only DRAM operation whose next row is known in advance, so merge the falling edge of row i with the rising edge of row i+1. A charge-sharing switch between the two local wordline drivers dumps about half of row i's ~3 V wordline charge into row i+1 before the VPP pump tops it up, and bitline precharge charge is likewise recycled across consecutive refreshes in a mat.
why: Attacks refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit, Fact 3) and the wordline CV^2 floor (Fact 10): ~30-45% less VPP pump energy per refresh, amplified because charge pumps run at only ~30% efficiency.

title: MoS2 grown on trench sidewalls: channel geometry set by depth
idea: Mo: etch DUV-pitch trenches and grow monolayer MoS2 conformally by MOCVD on the vertical sidewalls; each sidewall becomes a vertical 2D access channel whose length equals the step height, and an ALD gate fills the trench, giving two cells per DUV feature.
why: Doubles effective cell density per DUV pitch without EUV (fact 4), while the 0.65 nm body suppresses short-channel leakage (fact 3).

title: Per-row programmable Vt via charge-trap layer in the wordline stack
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: make a fixed property adjustable. A thin SiN charge-trap layer in the buried-wordline gate stack lets each row's access-transistor Vt be programmed by Fowler-Nordheim pulses at test and retrimmed in the field: leaky rows get ~+200 mV of Vt, strong rows keep low Vt for speed.
why: Compresses the retention distribution so refresh is set by a trimmed tail (Fact 3): 3-5x longer refresh interval without a global speed penalty.

title: Capacitor-first, transistor-last cell with high-temperature dielectric anneal
idea: Reverse the process order: build and crystallize the storage capacitor first (rutile TiO2 or SrTiO3 annealed at 700-800 C for k~70-100), then bond a thin single-crystal Si layer on top and form the access transistor with laser or microwave anneal so the capacitor is never reheated. The transistor never sees the capacitor's thermal budget, and the capacitor never has to tolerate the transistor's.
why: Charge wall (fact 1) and retention (fact 3): k~70+ gives ~2x Cs at today's aspect ratio, and a top-side transistor has no storage-node-to-substrate junction; ~2-4x longer refresh interval.

title: Mechanical switch: vertical NEMS contact replaces the access transistor
idea: Reverse what moves: instead of gating electrons through a semiconductor, the wordline electrostatically pulls a ~10 nm-gap vertical nanocantilever (Ru- or TiN-coated) into contact with the storage node. When open the gap is vacuum or gas, so off-state leakage is essentially zero and retention is limited only by capacitor dielectric leakage (minutes to hours).
why: Eliminates the access-transistor leakage tail and refresh (fact 3) and allows a low actuation voltage via nanogap; contact endurance of ~1e15 cycles is the core risk.

title: Decay-clock sensing: reference voltage tracks time since last restore
idea: Worse: assume worst-case decayed charge on every read so the margin is gone early. Flip: keep a coarse per-row refresh-epoch counter and set the sense-amp reference from a replica cell aged the same amount, so a stored '1' can decay to ~30% instead of ~60% before misreading.
why: Leakage-limited retention (fact 3): 2-3x longer refresh interval without touching the access transistor.

title: Magnetostrictive-squeezed Mott switch from delay-line wire technology
idea: Revive the magnetostrictive nickel-wire delay line: wordline current through a Galfenol (Fe-Ga) strip strains an adjacent nanoscale piezoresistive Mott material (SmSe-class) into its metallic phase, opening the cell. With no current the material relaxes to its insulating phase, ~1e5x more resistive, and there is no semiconductor junction to leak.
why: Isolation comes from a band-gapped insulator at zero strain rather than a subthreshold MOSFET (fact 3); galvanic separation between wordline and channel also removes wordline-coupling row-hammer paths (fact 9).

title: Bell Labs electret back-gate holds access devices deeply off
idea: Revive Sessler and West's 1962 Bell Labs foil electret: implant a permanent negative trapped-charge layer, charged by corona or electron beam, into the Al2O3/SiO2 buried oxide under thin-body access transistors. This gives a built-in ~1 V reverse back bias with no charge pump, on U.S. FD-SOI lines; a boosted front-gate pulse restores on-current.
why: Raises hold Vt with no bias-generation power or periphery (facts 3, 7), cutting subthreshold leakage 10-100x.

title: Hemoglobin-cooperative Mott switch in series with access FET
idea: Hemoglobin binds O2 with Hill coefficient ~3, almost all-or-nothing; add a thin NbO2 insulator-metal-transition element in series with the access transistor's bitline contact so the composite stays insulating at retention bias (<VARY/2) and snaps metallic only when the wordline-driven current crosses the IMT threshold.
why: Composite off-current is set by the Mott insulator, ~1e4x below FET subthreshold leakage, giving seconds of retention; the abrupt turn-on preserves on-current without extra VPP.

title: Gate-triggered Mott-gap channel gives access device without subthreshold tail
idea: Effect: filling-controlled Mott transition. The access channel is a correlated oxide (e.g., electron-doped SmNiO3 or Ca2RuO4) where the wordline field adds ~0.1 carrier per site and collapses the Mott gap abruptly; below critical filling it is a gapped insulator whose leakage scales as exp(-Eg/kT) instead of following a gradual subthreshold slope.
why: Leakage tail and voltage floor (facts 3, 10): an abrupt switch allows wordline swing ~1.5 V instead of 3 V (~4x less wordline CV2) while holding <1 aA, removing most refresh.

title: Solar-cell fixed-charge passivation spacer on the storage junction
idea: Borrow PERC/TOPCon solar-cell field-effect passivation: put a SiNx/AlOx spacer with engineered fixed charge (positive next to the n+ storage node) over the storage-junction surface. The surface stays accumulated, so surface SRH generation and the GIDL fringe field are suppressed.
why: The solar industry cut surface recombination velocity ~100x this way. Here it targets the surface-generation share of junction leakage, aiming for a 3-5x tail reduction with tools already in high-volume solar fabs.

title: Mott NDR load-line bistable cell keeps data without refresh
idea: Box: small node cap x one access transistor plus one NbO2 Mott or Si/SiGe Esaki NDR element tied to a hold rail x SA x vertically stacked over the transistor x Si x ALD + anneal. The NDR load line intersecting the leakage line gives two stable node voltages, so leakage self-corrects instead of decaying (tunnel-SRAM idea at ~1T footprint).
why: Eliminates refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) entirely; standby set by NDR valley current (target <1 pA/cell). Needs high peak-to-valley ratio at nm scale.

title: Decaying reference cells make sense threshold slide with leakage
idea: Po: the reference forgets as fast as the data. Each subarray carries reference cells written to a half level at the same time as the row and sharing its well, so they leak at the same rate; the sense amp compares against this decaying reference instead of a fixed VBL/2, so a decayed 1 still reads correctly long after it crossed the fixed midpoint.
why: Fact 3: sensing margin, not total charge loss, sets retention; a tracking reference extends usable retention 2-3x and cuts refresh energy and bandwidth tax proportionally.

title: Split-gate vertical access device with floating mid-node stack effect
idea: IFR: leakage finds no voltage to push it. Split the vertical access channel into two gate segments driven by the same wordline with a short doped mid-node between them; in the off state the mid-node floats to an intermediate voltage so each segment sees small Vds, negative Vgs on the upper segment and no DIBL.
why: Fact 3: the series stack effect cuts subthreshold and GIDL leakage ~10-30x with no footprint cost in a vertical cell, extending refresh interval proportionally.

title: Shop-door air curtain: electrostatically doped storage junction with no dopant atoms
idea: An air curtain separates indoors from outdoors with no physical door. Form the storage-node 'n+ region' electrostatically: a low-workfunction metal contact (hafnium- or yttrium-based) on an undoped silicon tip induces an electron layer by workfunction difference, so there is no implanted junction, no dopant clusters and no BF2 or fluorine co-implant.
why: Without implanted dopants and their damage, generation sites and random-dopant Vt variation shrink, narrowing the leakage tail (fact 3) and removing implant steps (fact 4).

title: T-RAM fixed: electrostatically doped thyristor erases dopant variability
idea: T-RAM Semiconductor's thin-capacitively-coupled thyristor died on the spread of its latch and holding voltages, caused by random implanted p-n-p-n doping. Build the thyristor in an undoped silicon nanosheet and induce its four regions with split gates (electrostatic doping). The controller trims the latch threshold per bank after test by setting gate voltages. Run the cell in dynamic mode, so data is stored as base charge rather than as holding current.
why: Removes both killers of thyristor RAM, variability and standby current. The result is a ~1-2 ns gain-read cell with no capacitor (attacks the capacitor wall), and base-charge refresh is claimed to be needed ~100x less often than DRAM refresh.

title: Convert idle 3D NAND fabs into DRAM-class tier lines
idea: IFR: the factory already exists and is paid for. Retool underused, depreciated 3D NAND fabs, whose channel-hole etch, ALD and staircase tools are the same ones needed, to make deposition-defined DRAM-class cells (short-retention charge-trap or oxide gain-cell tiers), with joint ventures that give NAND makers a DRAM-priced product.
why: Constraint: depreciation is ~55% of DRAM wafer cost (fact 4); stacked cells on paid-off NAND tools give ~10x bits per wafer at NAND wafer cost and add supply in 12-18 months, not 3-5 years.

title: Lattice-matched GaP storage-node contact blocks band-to-band tunneling
idea: Effect: heterojunction band offset. A few-nm epitaxial GaP layer (0.4% lattice mismatch to Si, Eg 2.26 eV) at the gate-overlapped storage-node contact forces GIDL tunneling across a wider gap (rate ~exp(-Eg^1.5/F)), cutting GIDL by up to ~10^3. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): GIDL dominates at negative wordline hold bias; claims 4x internal refresh skip. Risk: Ga cross-contamination in a DRAM line.

title: Sparse neural coding keeps most cells in the non-leaking state
idea: Cortex fires sparsely to save energy; encode each word with an inversion flag (or a low-weight 8b/9b code, aware of true- and anti-cell polarity) so 60-70% of cells sit in the discharged state that cannot lose data, and skip refresh on rows whose code flags them all-discharged (zero pages).
why: Refresh and restore energy scale with charged cells, so they fall ~40-60%; skipping zero rows (10-30% of AI and VM memory) also recovers bandwidth.

title: Eliminate the semiconductor channel: NEM contact relay access switch
idea: Remove the transistor channel altogether and isolate each storage node with a nanoelectromechanical cantilever relay whose off state is a 5-10 nm air gap. The wordline electrostatically pulls the beam into contact for read/write; once released there is no subthreshold, junction or GIDL path, only gap tunneling (<1e-24 A).
why: Attacks the 13 fA leakage tail and refresh (fact 3): retention is bounded only by capacitor dielectric leakage, so refresh interval moves from 64 ms to minutes, removing most of the ~46 fJ/bit refresh energy and 10-20% bandwidth loss. Contact wear threatens unlimited endurance.

title: Bootstrapped guard node gives the inner switch zero voltage to leak
idea: TRIZ #12 Equipotentiality (the electrometer guard trick): put two access transistors in series and drive their middle node from a source follower whose gate is the storage node. In retention the inner transistor sees ~0 V across it and leaks almost nothing, while all leakage from the bitline is absorbed by the actively driven guard node.
why: Subthreshold current scales as (1 - exp(-Vds/kT)), so holding Vds ~ 0 gives ~100x lower leakage (Fact 3): seconds-scale retention for a 3T cell, trading some density for refresh-free cache/HBM tiers.

title: Biologist's DNA proofreading: early-warning margin reads before cells fail
idea: Cells repair DNA lesions before they become mutations. A background scrubber reads each row with the sense-amp reference deliberately shifted ~30% of signal toward the decayed level; rows whose ECC syndrome changes under the shifted read are flagged 'damaged' and refreshed now, while rows that stay clean have their own refresh period doubled step by step, up to 1 s.
why: Refresh is set by the worst row at the worst temperature; evidence-based per-row periods cut refresh operations 4-10x and catch variable-retention cells as they shift.

title: Two gates in series on one pillar: stack-effect leakage suppression
idea: Scale jump that folds logic's standby 'transistor stacking' trick into one vertical-channel access pillar with two independently driven gate segments (upper and lower wordline); both turn on for access, but in hold the intermediate node floats up a few hundred mV, putting the upper device at negative VGS with reduced DIBL.
why: Subthreshold leakage tail (fact 3): the stack effect cuts off-current 10-30x, enabling 4F^2 vertical cells with ~1 s retention.

title: Voltage-stacked subarray pairs halve refresh supply current
idea: Effect: series voltage stacking (charge conservation). Two subarrays refreshed together run in stacked domains, A between VDD and VDD/2 and B between VDD/2 and 0 with plates biased per domain, so the restore current drawn through A's sense amps is reused by B instead of returning to ground. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Refresh energy (fact 3): ~2x less supply charge per refreshed bit pair, with no external voltage change.

title: Erasure-coded decay: refresh only when information is at risk
idea: IFR: refresh happens only when information, not charge, is about to be lost. Store each page with a strong cross-row LDPC/erasure code and let cells decay; a background reader samples syndrome weight per page and re-encodes only pages nearing the correction limit.
why: Fact 3: the refresh interval is set by code tolerance instead of the worst cell, plausibly 10x fewer refreshes for ~6-12% parity overhead.

title: In-field wordline self-heating anneal heals variable-retention traps
idea: Box: standard cell x access transistor used as its own heater via ms high-current wordline pulses during idle x SA retention self-test x in-mat x Si x zero masks. Local ~200-300C channel micro-anneals relax metastable trap configurations behind variable retention time, then a self-test confirms the row.
why: VRT cells force conservative refresh margins; healing them in the field could extend refresh ~2x (fact 3). Thermal damage risk is speculative.

title: Astronomer's standard star: co-decaying ghost reference cells per row
idea: Astronomers correct for haze with a reference star in the same frame. Every row holds two ghost cells written at mid-charge whenever the row is written or refreshed; they leak alongside the data, and the sense amp uses their decayed level as the reference instead of a fixed VBL/2, so data stays readable after much more decay.
why: A fixed reference loses margin as stored '1's sag; a co-decaying reference roughly doubles to quadruples usable retention, cutting refresh energy and bandwidth 2-4x for <1% area.

title: Ten-year-equivalent stabilization bake plus per-die Vt trim fuses
idea: Worse at 125 C: ship access devices that will drift for years as defects relax. Flip: run a hot-bias stabilization bake equivalent to 10 years at 125 C during the BEOL anneal, then measure each die's leakage and blow eFuses that set its wordline-low and refresh trim to the post-drift value.
why: Removes lifetime drift guard-bands on leakage and refresh (fact 3), roughly 1.5-2x refresh savings.

title: Field-ionized deep-dopant extensions stay semi-insulating while holding
idea: Effect: Poole-Frenkel field-assisted ionization. Dope the storage-node-side extension with a deep donor (e.g., S or Se in Si, ~0.3 eV, kept away from midgap to avoid SRH generation) so it is mostly un-ionized and semi-insulating at the low hold field, but the wordline-on field lowers the barrier and ionizes it within picoseconds so the extension conducts.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): removes the field-enhanced junction path that dominates the <=13 fA tail; claims ~10x tail reduction. Risk: deep levels as generation centres.

title: Field-drifted mobile-ion Vt trim repairs weak cells at sort
idea: Effect: thermally activated ion migration. A sub-nm Cs-doped sublayer sits in the access gate dielectric; at wafer sort the tester biases only retention-failing rows at ~200 C so ions drift from the channel side to the gate side, raising those transistors' Vt ~0.1-0.2 V; high activation energy (~1.5 eV) freezes them for life at operating temperature. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): ppm weak rows join the bulk distribution, so internal refresh can follow the median; claims 4x refresh interval.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO gate stack buys 0.3 V higher access Vt
idea: Effect: ferroelectric negative capacitance. Insert a 3-4 nm HZO layer capacitance-matched to the buried-channel access transistor's gate oxide so the stack amplifies surface potential and swings below 60 mV/dec in the switching window; raise Vt ~0.3 V (up to ~5 decades less subthreshold current) while keeping on-current at equal or lower wordline voltage.
why: Leakage tail and voltage floor (facts 3, 10): 10-100x retention, or wordline from 3 V to ~2.2 V (~45% less wordline CV2).

title: Deliberately low-barrier MTJs as refreshed fast spin DRAM
idea: Po: a magnet that is supposed to forget. Design MTJ free layers with only ~25 kT energy barrier so bits flip spontaneously after ~10-100 ms; the low barrier cuts write current ~10x, so a minimum access device suffices, and bits are scrubbed on a DRAM-like refresh schedule.
why: Facts 1 and 10: no capacitor, low write voltage, ~10 fJ writes and effectively unlimited endurance since the barrier is never stressed; beyond prior nonvolatile MRAM.

title: Piezoelectronic pressure switch replaces silicon access transistor
idea: Box: MIM cap x piezoelectronic transistor (PMN-PT actuator squeezing a SmSe piezoresistive layer through its insulator-metal transition) x SA x BEOL stack x Si x sputter + anneal. The wordline drives the piezo, pressure drops channel resistance >1e4x; unpowered, the channel is a gapped insulator with no junction to leak.
why: Off-state set by an insulating phase rather than a subthreshold tail (fact 3, ~100x retention) and switching at ~0.1-0.2 V breaks the 3 V wordline floor (fact 10).

title: Micro-sense: one local amplifier per 16 cells
idea: Reverse the cell-to-amplifier ratio: instead of ~500 cells on a long bitline per sense amp, place a 3-4 transistor local preamp (CMOS under array) under every 16-cell local bitline, so bitline capacitance drops from ~50 fF to ~3 fF. The transfer ratio Cs/(Cs+Cbl) rises from ~0.1 to ~0.6, so a cell stays readable after losing far more of its charge.
why: Retention margin (facts 1, 3): tolerating 3-5x more charge loss lengthens refresh 3-5x at the same leakage, or permits a ~2 fF capacitor instead of chasing AR 115.

title: Piezoelectric liner strains the access channel during retention
idea: Wrap the buried wordline in an AlScN piezoelectric liner on a separate standby bias. While rows retain, the liner compresses the channel and strain raises Vt; strain is released for access.
why: A strain-tuned Vt shift of 50-100 mV gives 5-20x less leakage with no on-current penalty.

title: Buried piezoresistive stressor trades extra mobility for higher access Vt
idea: Effect: piezoresistance (strain-shifted conduction valleys). Wrap the buried-channel access transistor with a ~1.5 GPa tensile SiN or AlN liner, raising electron mobility 30-50%, then spend that drive on ~90 mV higher Vt, so write speed and VPP stay the same. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): ~1.5 decades less subthreshold leakage; die refreshes each row only every 2nd-4th REF internally.

title: Helical-channel vertical access transistor for long channels in 4F2
idea: Worse: shrink the channel until DIBL dominates leakage. Flip: wrap a screw-thread spiral channel around each pillar (tilted-ion spiral sidewall mask, then conformal channel deposition) so the effective gate length is 3-4x the pillar height in the same footprint.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): 10-100x lower off-current without area penalty; enables longer refresh or smaller Cs (fact 1).

title: Eliminate gate electrostatics: piezoelectric transduction switch as access device
idea: Replace the FET with a piezoelectronic transistor: a relaxor piezoelectric (PMN-PT) actuator squeezes a thin piezoresistive SmSe layer, driving an insulator-to-metal transition with 1e4-1e5 resistance change at ~0.1 V. The off state is a wide-gap insulator rather than a thermally populated channel.
why: Sub-0.2 V switching attacks the 1 V/3 V voltage floor (fact 10) and the insulating off state could cut leakage by orders of magnitude; materials integration risk is very high.

title: Space-CCD bakeout: on-die heaters anneal leakage traps in field
idea: Space telescopes periodically heat their CCDs to anneal radiation-induced traps. Embed resistive heaters in the package or under each bank and, after migrating data away, bake the array at ~150-200 C for minutes a few times a year to anneal variable-retention-time traps and re-passivate interface states.
why: Fact 3: the VRT and tail population that forces refresh guardbands grows with age; periodic anneal resets it, keeping refresh intervals long over life and cutting guardband ~2x.

title: Hibernation-latch ferroelectric gate: Vt parked high in deep idle
idea: Rosetta's spacecraft slept 31 months. Add a thin ferroelectric layer to the buried-wordline gate stack that is polarized only when a bank enters or leaves a long idle state (minutes to hours), shifting access Vt up ~0.4 V while hibernating and back when active; flips happen per hibernation, not per access, so ~1e6 cycles suffice.
why: Fact 3: idle banks of cold data (most server memory at any moment) get ~1e4 lower leakage and almost no refresh, without the endurance wall that ruled out per-access ferroelectric switching.

title: Negative-charge Al2O3 liner accumulates STI sidewalls against surface generation
idea: Borrow the passivation physics of PERC solar cells and backside-illuminated image sensors. Line the STI trenches next to storage nodes with 3-5 nm ALD Al2O3 carrying ~-3e12 cm^-2 fixed charge. This accumulates holes on the p-type sidewall and pushes the depletion region away from STI interface traps. Surface generation, which scales with Dit x n_i in depletion, falls by orders of magnitude once the surface is accumulated.
why: STI-edge cells are a known tail population. 10-100x lower surface generation gives ~4-10x longer worst-case retention for one ALD step and no new lithography (facts 3, 4).

title: Rutile-GeO2 ambipolar BEOL logic performs refresh locally per mat
idea: Ge: use rutile GeO2, an ultrawide-gap (~4.6 eV) oxide predicted to be both n- and p-dopable, to build complementary low-leakage transistors in the BEOL directly above each mat, hosting a tiny local refresh sequencer and restore driver so refresh never toggles global decoders, I/O or long data lines.
why: Takes refresh off the shared bus (fact 3: 10-20% bandwidth) and out of periphery area (fact 7); mats refresh in parallel, recovering most refresh bandwidth and ~30% of refresh energy.

title: Optical wordlines open dark-insulating photoconductive access pillars
idea: Effect: photoconductivity. Each storage capacitor reaches the bitline through a wide-gap photoconductor pillar (amorphous Se or ZnS, dark resistivity >10^13 ohm-cm, engineered short carrier lifetime for <10 ns turn-off); a row is opened by light from an on-die SiN waveguide grating, so the wordline is photons and the hold state is a dark insulator.
why: Leakage tail and periphery (facts 3, 7): attoamp dark current makes refresh near-zero; removes wordline drivers, row charge pumps and VPP from the ~49% periphery.

title: Modulation-doped In2O3/Ga2O3 superlattice channel resolves mobility versus leakage
idea: TRIZ #40 Composite materials: build the channel on glass as an ALD superlattice of ~1 nm In2O3 wells and Ga2O3 barriers, so electrons in the wells give high mobility when the gate fills them, while in the off state the wide-gap Ga2O3 barriers set the leakage floor and trap out oxygen-vacancy donors.
why: Breaks the drive-vs-leakage contradiction of single-composition oxides (Fact 3): target >30 cm2/Vs with <1e-20 A/um off-current, enabling 10-100 ns access on glass.

title: Minify refresh to nanowatts and feed it with a betavoltaic cell
idea: Pair hour-retention cells with a sleep-mode refresh interval of ~1 h and integrate a Ni-63 or tritium betavoltaic film on the package supplying microwatts for decades, so the module keeps its data alive after mains loss with no battery to wear out.
why: A 16 Gb die refreshed hourly needs ~0.2 uW (46 fJ/bit); volatile cells become effectively non-volatile with zero grid idle power.

title: Vinyl-record pressing: nanoimprint wordline gratings with diamond-like-carbon release, not fluorosilanes
idea: Records are stamped from a master in seconds instead of each being cut. Pattern dense wordline and active-line gratings by UV nanoimprint from a master mold coated with hydrogenated diamond-like carbon as the anti-stick layer, using a PFAS-free acrylate resist, O2 plasma descum and Cl2/HBr transfer etch in place of fluorosilane release layers and PFAS photoacid generators.
why: Cuts EUV/immersion passes and capital (fact 4); master-replicated lines avoid stochastic EUV line-edge roughness, narrowing the access-transistor Vt and leakage tail (fact 3).

title: CubeSat COTS mindset: half-charge capacitors in short 30:1 pillars
idea: CubeSats fly cheap commercial parts and absorb upsets in software. Size the cell capacitor for a 1% raw-BER sense margin (~2-2.5 fF) instead of ~5 fF, so pillar aspect ratio drops from ~65:1 to ~30:1 with standard high-k.
why: Fact 1: steps back from the capacitor charge wall; fewer deep-etch and deposition steps raise yield and cut cost, and short capacitors ease 3D tiers, with refresh at the 1% point roughly offsetting the lower charge.

title: Battery bit: store data as redox state, not loose charge
idea: Inverts 'a bit is free charge on a capacitor': each cell is a nanoscale solid-state redox couple (e.g., proton-intercalated WO3 against a reservoir) whose open-circuit potential encodes the bit; leakage only slowly shifts state of charge, and a gain transistor whose gate sits on the redox electrode reads it nondestructively.
why: Retention from ms to hours (fact 3) without a high-AR capacitor (fact 1); nondestructive read avoids rewrite energy (fact 8). Risks: 10-100 ns ion kinetics and endurance.

title: Charging-energy wall: Coulomb-blockade island as the leakage stopper
idea: Limit: leakage must be stopped by a quantum effect, not a barrier height. Put a sub-2 nm silicon or metal nanocrystal island in series with the access channel. Its charging energy (>0.5 eV) blocks single-electron transit until the wordline shifts the island level into resonance, and co-tunneling leakage is exponentially suppressed.
why: Fact 3: the off-state is set by the charging energy (~20 kT), not by doping or trap statistics, which could collapse the tail distribution. Speculative: island uniformity at room temperature.

title: Automotive e-coat bath self-plugs capacitor dielectric pinholes
idea: Before the top electrode goes on, immerse the array in an electrophoretic polymer/oxide paint bath and bias the bottom electrodes. Only pinholes and thin spots conduct, so insulating deposit grows exactly there and stops itself, just as car-body e-coat seals only the exposed metal.
why: Retention tail from dielectric leakage: plugging the weak spots could cut those tail cells ~5x and allow ~10-15% thinner high-k for more Cs at the same leakage.

title: 1.5 nm quantum-confined silicon access sheet widens effective band gap
idea: Effect: quantum confinement. Thin the vertical access channel to ~1.5 nm Si so subband confinement raises the effective gap from 1.12 to ~1.6-1.8 eV, cutting band-to-band GIDL and SRH generation (proportional to ni ~ exp(-Eg/2kT)) by up to ~10^4 at the storage junction.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): 10-100x retention, compatible with 4F2 vertical-channel cells. Risk: Vt variation ~1/t^2 and mobility loss.

title: Pumped-hydro operator: stepwise tank-capacitor wordline charging
idea: A pumped-hydro plant lifts water in stages and recovers it on the way down. Each wordline driver steps its line through 8 intermediate rails held by shared on-die tank capacitors (0, VPP/8 ... VPP) and steps it down the same way, returning charge to each tank.
why: Stepwise charging divides the CV^2 dissipation by the step count; 8 steps plus fewer pump-supplied coulombs cut wordline energy ~8-12x per access using standard transistors.

title: VO2 hyper-FET access transistor gives sub-60 mV per decade switching
idea: V: place a Ge-doped VO2 film (insulator-metal transition raised above ~100 C) in series with each access transistor's bitline contact; once the gate turns on, current triggers the abrupt IMT, giving an effective subthreshold slope of a few mV/decade, so Vt can sit higher at the same on-current and wordline voltage.
why: Breaks the 60 mV/dec link between leakage and wordline voltage (facts 3, 10): either ~10^3 less off-current at the same VPP or ~0.5-1 V lower wordline boost.

title: Printed-electronics bust fixed by toll-printing memory foil on converters
idea: The 2008-2012 printed-electronics boom went bust because startups built their own lines to make low-value labels. Instead, license a memory-foil recipe (printed oxide access devices plus capacitors) to U.S. flexible-packaging converters whose roll-to-roll lines run below capacity, and pay them per m2 of good foil.
why: Near-zero capital per unit of capacity because it uses idle presses, so supply can scale fast. Low-leakage printed access devices make the foil refresh-light, so it ships with only a simple controller.

title: RCA Selectron flood-gun holding rebuilt as optically held printed cells
idea: RCA's Selectron used a continuous flood electron beam to hold every bit (secondary emission made two potentials stable), but the tubes could not be manufactured. Print each cell as a storage node with two organic photoconductors that the node's own voltage gates, giving positive feedback. A uniform low-power LED flood then continuously restores both 1s and 0s, with no row cycling and no sense amps.
why: Refresh is replaced by photonic holding: no refresh commands, no bandwidth tax, no refresh periphery. The photoconductor stacks are printed.

title: Resonant LC wordline driver recycles refresh switching energy
idea: Effect: LC resonance and adiabatic charging. During internal refresh bursts, wordlines swing through an interposer or RDL spiral inductor resonating with the wordline capacitance, returning charge to the tank instead of dumping it to ground; the burst still fits inside today's tRFC. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Voltage floor and refresh energy (facts 3, 10): recovers 50-70% of 3 V wordline CV2, cutting refresh energy ~25-40%.

title: Kelvin curb-sending write pulses that cancel high-k dielectric soakage
idea: Revive Lord Kelvin's 1860s 'curb sender' for the transatlantic cable and the analog designers' dielectric-absorption compensation: each write or restore pulse gets a calibrated overshoot followed by a short reverse curb, pre-charging the slow Curie-von Schweidler polarization of the ZrO2/HfO2 storage capacitor. The apparent charge loss in the first milliseconds after a write, which today eats retention margin, goes away.
why: High-k relaxation removes a few percent of signal after each write and shows up as lost retention margin (facts 1, 3); recovering 5-10% of signal could stretch the refresh interval ~1.5-2x with only driver-timing changes.

title: Eliminate the storage-node junction: electrostatically induced virtual drain
idea: Delete the n+ storage-node implant: a thin, always-biased spacer gate (polarity gate) induces an electron layer that acts as the drain, so there is no metallurgical junction under the gate edge for band-to-band tunneling. The storage node contacts the induced layer through a silicide.
why: GIDL and junction trap-assisted tunneling dominate the retention tail (fact 3); removing the junction field peak could cut tail leakage 10-100x and stretch the refresh period 4-10x.

title: Thousand-times-leakier cells tamed by a refresh engine per tile
idea: Inverts 'access transistors must leak <=13 fA': use the cheapest stackable access devices (unannealed sputtered poly-Si or oxide TFTs leaking ~10 pA) so retention is only ~10-100 us, and put a micro-sense-amp under each 4k-cell tile (CMOS-under-array) that refreshes its own tile continuously without touching global bitlines.
why: Trades refresh energy (~3-5x today) for ~100x lower cost per GB from low-temperature, 2-mask tiers with no deep capacitor; refresh traffic never leaves the tile, so bandwidth is unaffected.

title: AlScN shadow layer parks idle rows non-volatilely when hot
idea: Worse at 125 C: keep refreshing idle data at the 4-8x hot refresh rate, or use HZO backup that depolarizes. Flip: put a wurtzite AlScN ferroelectric capacitor layer (Curie point >1000 C) under each mat; rows idle beyond N ms are copied into it and their DRAM refresh stops, so the low AlScN endurance is spent only on rare parks.
why: Hot idle refresh energy (fact 3) down 10x+; retention guaranteed over 10 years at 125 C.

title: Foveated rendering for memory: refresh low-order mantissa bit-planes far less
idea: VR headsets render full detail only where the eye looks. Store AI weights and KV caches bit-plane-wise so sign, exponent and top mantissa bits live in normally refreshed rows, while the lowest 3-5 mantissa bits of BF16/FP8 sit in rows refreshed 8-16x less often and are allowed rare flips.
why: For LLM-dominated DRAM, 30-50% of stored bits tolerate occasional errors; cuts refresh energy and bandwidth loss ~30-45% at 32-64 Gb (fact 3).

title: Best-effort memory cloud instances priced like spot capacity
idea: Offer a cloud instance class whose memory runs at 4-8x relaxed refresh, optionally on salvaged or second-life DRAM, at ~40% lower price. Guests see it as 'best-effort RAM' with a poison-page signal. Target workloads that checkpoint or recompute, such as ML training with frequent checkpoints, caches and batch analytics. A neocloud can pilot it on a few racks for <$1M within 24 months.
why: Turns the retention guardband into a priced product tier, lowering the effective cost per usable bit and stretching scarce DRAM supply (fact 3, cost per bit).

title: Asymmetric gate oxide: thick on storage side, thin on bitline side
idea: Worse at 125 C: use a uniformly thin gate oxide that suffers stress-induced leakage and GIDL after years hot. Flip: grow a graded gate oxide (selective re-oxidation at the storage-node end of the recess) so the storage edge sees ~2x the thickness and ~3x lower field while the bitline side keeps drive current.
why: GIDL and SILC leakage (fact 3) down 10x and stable over a 10-year 125 C life.

title: Energy Star for memory: label DIMMs by idle refresh watts
idea: Revive the EPA's 1992 Energy Star program, which pushed PCs into sleep modes: create an Energy Star memory tier based on measured self-refresh watts per GB at 45 C, and require the top tier in federal procurement, rewarding low-leakage access devices from U.S. fabs.
why: Creates market pull for cutting refresh energy (fact 3), which is 16-33% of idle memory power, and steers U.S. data-center buying.

title: Antifuse redundancy sized for one-second retention binning
idea: Run deep retention tests on 1990s ATE to find rows failing a 1 s retention target. Antifuses remap them to an enlarged spare pool (3-5% spare rows), and the part ships with a 1 s refresh.
why: Refresh energy falls ~94% for a few percent of area.

title: Eliminate implant damage: molecular monolayer doping for access junctions
idea: Form storage-node and bitline junctions by grafting a phosphorus- or arsenic-bearing molecular monolayer onto silicon, capping it and driving in by rapid thermal anneal, giving ultra-shallow junctions with no ion-implant end-of-range defects. Implant-induced deep traps are a key source of the trap-assisted junction leakage tail.
why: Fewer deep-level traps tighten the retention tail (fact 3) and remove the need for an implanter (capital); wet chemistry plus RTA only.

title: Rolltronics plastic failure fixed with roll-to-roll flexible glass anneal
idea: Rolltronics' roll-to-roll a-Si TFTs on plastic died on substrate shrinkage and the low process temperatures plastic allows. Build oxide access TFTs on rolls of ~100 um flexible glass, which tolerate 450 C anneals. Those anneals drive out the oxygen vacancies and hydrogen that set the oxide-TFT leakage tail.
why: Hot-annealed oxide channels are claimed to have a 10-100x tighter leakage tail than plastic-limited ones, which makes refresh-free printed memory foils credible.

title: HFT-overclocker truncated restore: cut tRAS, let weak cells fail
idea: High-frequency traders overclock and accept margins others refuse. Shorten the restore phase of activate and refresh (tRAS and tWR ~30-40% shorter) so slow tail access transistors leave cells partly charged; the code absorbs the resulting ~1% errors, and partly restored rows are queued to refresh first.
why: Facts 3 and 8: lower access latency and ~30% less refresh time and restore energy, recovering refresh bandwidth and row-cycle time with no device change.

title: Lost-wax helical channel packs a 60 nm gate into 12 nm footprint
idea: Deposit a sacrificial carbon helix in the pillar hole by glancing-angle spiral deposition, wrap it with gate dielectric and metal, burn the carbon out (lost-wax casting), then ALD-backfill the helical void with the channel. The result is a gate-all-around helix with L~60 nm in a vertical cell.
why: Fact 3: long L kills DIBL and short-channel subthreshold leakage by orders of magnitude, so VT can be lowered and wordline voltage dropped (fact 10) while retention rises ~10x. The cost is on-current, offset by the GAA helix width.

title: Charge-transfer pre-sensing lets cells lose 80 percent of charge
idea: Today the cell's ~30,000 electrons are diluted onto a ~50 fF bitline to give ~100 mV, yet the kT/C noise of a 2 fF node is only ~1.4 mV. Hold the bitline at a fixed potential with a transfer gate biased at threshold, so the cell's charge is funneled onto a ~2 fF sense node. This revives the 1970s charge-transfer amplifier with modern offset cancellation and multiplies the signal ~20x.
why: If 20% of the original charge is enough for a reliable read, retention = dQ/I grows ~4-5x with no change in leakage. Refresh energy and bandwidth fall in proportion (facts 1, 3).

title: Charge-transfer pre-sensing resolves half-decayed cells within tRCD
idea: Effect: charge transfer through a subthreshold-biased MOSFET (CCD floating-diffusion style). A charge-transfer preamplifier between bitline and sense amp funnels bitline charge onto a small sense node, multiplying signal ~5-10x by C_BL/C_sense, so cells that have lost ~70% of their charge still resolve. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Retention criterion (facts 1, 3): time-to-fail lengthens 2-3x for the same leakage, so internal refresh halves.

title: Minify oxide damage: write floating gates with photons, not fields
idea: Program floating-gate cells by internal photoemission: an on-chip waveguide delivers ~3.5 eV photons that lift electrons over a thick 8 nm SiO2 barrier at low field, so the oxide never sees the high-field stress that limits flash to ~1e5 cycles; hole photoemission erases. The thick oxide gives 10-year retention.
why: Non-volatile, refresh-free, potentially 1e12+ endurance; write speed set by optical power per row with full-row parallel writes.

title: Vertical crosspoint TFT: 1T1C cell with two masks per layer
idea: IFR: the cell is just the place where two lines cross. At each bitline/wordline crossing, a vertical oxide-semiconductor channel grows in a self-aligned via through the wordline, which wraps it as the gate, and a small pad on top is the storage node facing a common plate film; each layer needs only two non-EUV masks.
why: Constraint: true 4F^2 1T1C per layer with full transistor isolation, and eight cheap stacked layers give ~12x density versus 6F^2 at near-equal wafer cost.

title: Lattice-matched GaP storage-node junction moves depletion into wide-gap material
idea: P (as GaP): selectively regrow a thin n+ GaP contact (2.26 eV gap, only 0.4% lattice mismatch to Si) on the silicon access transistor so the junction depletion region, where SRH generation happens, sits in GaP with ~10^7x lower intrinsic carrier density, while the channel stays silicon.
why: SRH junction leakage is proportional to n_i (fact 3); relocating even part of the depletion region into GaP could cut junction leakage by orders of magnitude while keeping silicon drive current.

title: Coulomb-blockade island chain as a leak-proof access channel on quartz
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation, taken to the extreme: segment the access channel into a chain of 1-2 nm nanocrystal islands self-assembled on a quartz or sapphire substrate (no silicon wafer). In the off state the single-electron charging energy (>> kT at room temperature for <2 nm islands) blocks transport exponentially with chain length; the wordline gate lifts the blockade for access.
why: Leakage is set by charging energy rather than doping or bandgap (Fact 3): theoretical off-current far below 1e-21 A for hours of retention; bottom-up assembly avoids EUV (Fact 4).

title: Vehicle history report: retention passport and stress odometer per die
idea: Adapted from vehicle history reports and odometers: each die keeps a write-protected record of its factory retention bins and weak-cell map, plus counters for hot hours, activations and refresh-error events, readable by any refurbisher through a standard command.
why: Retention testing a used module takes hours at temperature, which kills reuse economics; a trusted passport lets refurbishers re-grade modules in seconds and set safe second-life refresh rates (fact 3).

title: Substitute hydrogen forming gas with deuterium-in-nitrogen anneal
idea: Substitute the H2/N2 (or argon-diluted) forming-gas anneal with high-pressure D2 in N2 after BEOL. Si-D bonds at access-transistor interfaces resist field- and hot-carrier-driven depassivation ~10x better (kinetic isotope effect), so fewer traps form over the part's life. No rare gas is used at any step.
why: Attacks variable retention time and aging of the leakage tail: a tighter tail over life allows 1.5-3x more refresh margin and less guardband.

title: Bearing-style selective assembly pairs leaky arrays with tight sense amps
idea: In a CMOS-bonded-array flow, map each array wafer's retention and each periphery wafer's sense-amp offset before hybrid bonding. Then pair dies by measurement, as bearing makers match graded balls to races, so the leakiest arrays get the lowest-offset sense amps.
why: Retention spec equals charge loss vs sense margin. Matched pairing could lift the worst-case refresh interval ~1.5-2x and raise sellable yield without any process change.

title: Rad-hard SOI trick: buried plate swung negative in standby
idea: Satellite SOI chips tune transistors through the substrate; build the array over a buried plate (SOI or deep n-well) under all access channels and drive it to about -2 V whenever a subarray idles, raising Vt ~150-200 mV, then to 0 to +0.5 V when the bank opens to boost drive current.
why: Fact 3: ~10-50x lower subthreshold leakage in idle subarrays lengthens refresh intervals by a similar factor, and active-mode forward bias lets the access device shrink; cost is the plate charging energy per bank open.

title: ESI laser trimming revived to heal weak access transistors
idea: Revive 1970s Portland-made laser trimming of resistors: after a retention test, a U.S.-built infrared picosecond laser fires through backside-thinned silicon to anneal the gate region of the ppm-level worst-leakage cells, healing trap clusters and raising each die's retention floor.
why: The refresh interval is set by the worst few cells (fact 3); repairing the bottom 1e-6 of the tail could stretch tREFW 2-4x.

title: Retread DRAM: remanufactured modules sold with per-row retention maps
idea: Like tire retreading, take DRAM from decommissioned servers, re-characterize each row's retention at temperature, and write the map into the SPD. Resell the modules for tiers whose controllers apply per-row refresh rates.
why: Raises usable supply during shortage. Per-row refresh on mapped modules cuts refresh energy 2-4x versus blanket rates.

title: Eliminate the semiconductor: ALD MIIM tunnel-diode 1D1C cell
idea: Isolate each capacitor with a metal-insulator-insulator-metal diode (ALD Al2O3/Ta2O5 between dissimilar work-function metals) whose step-tunneling barrier gives ~1e6 nonlinearity; cells are crosspoint-addressed by V/2 biasing, and at hold bias tunneling is exponentially suppressed. Every layer is a university ALD or sputter step.
why: No crystalline silicon or dopants, BEOL-stackable for many tiers (fact 2); retention hinges on reaching <1e-17 A at half-select.

title: LN2-immersion memory pods with 77K-retuned low-Vt access transistors
idea: Borrowing from cryo-CMOS built for quantum-computer control, retune the access transistor for 77 K: subthreshold slope steepens from ~80 to ~20 mV/dec, so Vt can drop ~0.4 V and the wordline from ~3 V to ~1.5 V while off-current still falls >1000x. DIMMs run immersed in boiling liquid nitrogen (made from air, no chokepoint) with refresh stretched from 64 ms to minutes.
why: Facts 3 and 10: refresh tax (16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth) goes to near zero and wordline CV^2 roughly quarters; cryoplant overhead must stay below the saving, which favors large AI memory pods.

title: Galvanized sacrificial hydrogen reservoir re-passivates traps over lifetime
idea: Place a hydrogen-rich SiNx:H liner next to the access channel as a galvanizing-style sacrificial layer. It slowly releases H to re-passivate interface traps as they depassivate in service, much as zinc corrodes first to protect steel.
why: Lifetime retention drift and VRT growth: keeps the tail near time-zero quality, avoiding end-of-life refresh-rate derating.

title: Reference cells that decay alongside their row
idea: Flip the sensing reference from a fixed VARY/2 to a moving one: each row carries a '1' and a '0' reference cell written at the same instant as the data and leaking through identical devices, and their charge-shared average becomes that row's sense threshold. As stored '1's sag, the threshold follows them down instead of waiting for them to cross a fixed midpoint.
why: Retention (fact 3): tracking common-mode decay tolerates ~2x more charge loss, giving ~1.5-2x longer refresh for ~0.03% area (2 cells per 8k).

title: Deuterium-only process plus hydrogen barrier for oxide-channel access devices
idea: Worse at 125 C: leave process hydrogen free to diffuse into an oxide-semiconductor channel and shift Vt. Flip: run every deposition with deuterated precursors (D2O, SiD4), seal the array with ALD Al2O3/SiN and a Ti getter ring, so the remaining isotope moves slower and binds more strongly.
why: Makes oxide-channel low-leakage devices (fact 3) survive 10 years at 125 C with less than 50 mV drift.

title: LC-resonant adiabatic refresh spends refresh's spare time, not energy
idea: A normal restore dissipates ~CV^2 because bitlines and wordlines are slammed in ~10 ns, yet refresh has a 64 ms window. Drive refresh-only activations with ~1 us ramps from an on-package LC tank or N-step tank capacitors. Dissipation then follows (RC/T)*CV^2, and most of the charge returns to the supply.
why: With T/RC ~50-100, the switching part of the ~46 fJ/bit refresh energy drops ~10x. That attacks refresh's 16-33% share of idle power (fact 3) without touching the cell.

title: Test-floor laser anneal heals individual leaky-tail cells
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x retention test map x post-test die-level repair x Si x picosecond green laser through a BEOL window, like laser fuse repair. Retention test locates the ~0.01% tail cells and a localized pulse anneals trap clusters in that cell's junction, moving it into the main distribution instead of swapping it with redundancy.
why: Tail cells set the 64 ms interval; healing them extends refresh 2-4x (50-75% less refresh energy, fact 3) and frees redundancy area. Reaching the junction through the metal stack is the risk.

title: Canary cells: deliberately weak cells decide when to refresh
idea: Inverts 'refresh is scheduled for the worst cell at the worst temperature': each mat carries a few canary cells built with a 2-3x wider access device (predictably leakier than any real cell) and a continuous-time comparator; a mat is refreshed only when its canary crosses threshold, tracking local temperature, voltage and aging.
why: Most mats retain >=10x longer than spec (fact 3); local triggering cuts average refresh energy and bandwidth loss ~4-8x without per-row profiling tables.

title: Bell Labs CCD memory revived: charge rings with one regenerator
idea: Revive the 1970s CCD serial memories (invented at Bell Labs in 1969, later sold as CCD RAMs): store bits as charge packets in gated MOS potential wells with no per-bit contact or junction, arranged in short rings that pass one regeneration amplifier. Build them at relaxed nodes on U.S. CCD and imager fab processes.
why: There is no per-bit access transistor or junction leakage path (fact 3), refresh happens naturally as charge circulates, and few contacts means lighter lithography (fact 4). Latency of ~100 ns to 1 us makes it a capacity tier.

title: Film-capacitor self-clearing: a pulse burns out each leakage path
idea: Adapted from self-clearing metallized film capacitors, whose thin electrode vaporizes around a breakdown spot to isolate it: make the storage-node top electrode an ultrathin film and apply a controlled clearing pulse to cells that test leaky, so the electrode opens or oxidizes locally at the leakage path while the rest keeps most of the capacitance.
why: Turns dielectric leakage defects in the tail (facts 1, 3) into repairable events at test or in the field rather than row replacement or faster refresh; a cleared cell keeps working with slightly lower capacitance.

title: Ceramic-glazed wide-gap heterojunction skin on the storage-node junction
idea: Like a glaze fired onto pottery, grow a 2-3 nm lattice-matched wide-gap crystal skin (e.g., GaP or AlP on Si, Eg ~2.3-2.5 eV) only on the storage-node side of the access channel. Band-to-band tunneling and GIDL must then cross a wide gap.
why: GIDL is a dominant tail mechanism under high storage voltage and wordline-low bias. BTBT falls roughly with exp(-Eg^1.5), so >100x less GIDL leakage could stretch refresh intervals several-fold.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembled 3 nm nanowires widen bandgap by confinement
idea: Use block-copolymer self-assembly (no litho) to define 3-4 nm vertical Si nanowire access channels. Quantum confinement raises the effective gap to ~1.6-2 eV, exponentially suppressing BTBT/GIDL and intrinsic generation.
why: Facts 3 and 4: wider effective gap could cut junction/GIDL leakage 10-100x and removes an EUV layer. Series resistance and diameter variability are the risks.

title: Horticultural grafting of a crystalline silicon film onto the capacitor array
idea: Grafting joins a separately grown scion to a rootstock; dope and activate a crystalline Si layer on a donor wafer at high temperature, bond it onto the finished capacitor array with a <=350 C Smart-Cut split, and only then pattern access transistors aligned to the landing pads below, using pre-activated or junctionless doping.
why: Gets FEOL-quality low-leakage channels above capacitors made with materials that cannot see >400 C (k~70 perovskites, Ru electrodes), separating the transistor and capacitor thermal budgets and enabling 3D tiers.
